newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Funds sought to demobilise 100,000 Angolans.
newsitem.headline: Funds sought to demobilise 100,000 Angolans.

text.p: Demobilisation of 100,000 soldiers in Angola -- and with it the peace process that ended two decades of civil war -- is in jeopardy due to a lack of funds, an aid agency said on Friday.

The International Organisation for Migration (IOM) appealed to Western donors for $38 million to finance its six-month programme to demobilise and transport home 100,000 soldiers accompanied by their 340,000 dependents.
Since 1996, the Geneva-based agency has transported 3,272 ex-combattants and their 1,194 dependents. The total of 4,466 people represents just one per cent of the overall caseload.

"Finally, after many delays, demobilisation is going ahead and seems to be increasing in pace," Peter Schatzer, IOM's director of external relations, told a news briefing. "We have to address now this funding shortage very seriously."

"If funds are not coming through then this would jeopardise the demobilisation operation and in turn probably the whole peace process," he added. "Angola is just a neighbour to Zaire and destabilisation in Angola wouldn't help this part of the world either."
Funds will be used to cover the cost of transportation, medical services, and provision of reintegration kits.
Donor countries have given about $14 million over the last two years toward the demobilisation effort, but IOM's cash reserve will run out at the end of April unless funds arrive.

A 1994 peace accord ended nearly two decades of civil war between the ruling Popular Movement for the Liberation of Angola (MPLA) and former rebels of the National Union for the Total Independence of Angola (UNITA).

"In a country as vast as Angola, and with the tremendous (anti-personnel) mine problem, we cannot move people as cheaply as in Mozambique. We have tremendous logistical problems to get people home," Schatzer told Reuters.
Demobilisation was due to start in Loduimbali (Huambo province) on Friday, followed by N'gove (Benguela province) and and Chicuma (Huila province) on Monday, according to IOM.
James Purcell, IOM's director, will make a four-day trip to Angola from Monday to discuss demobilisation with officials from the national unity government inaugurated two weeks ago.
He will also meet with donor country officials to seek significant financial support for demobilisation, IOM said.
